patients with CIPN from eight national cancer insti-
tutes. Initially, 231 patients were divided randomly into
two arms [39]. One group received 60 mg Duloxetine
daily for the initial 5-week treatment and then a placebo
during the crossover period. On the contrary, the other
group received a placebo in their first treatment period.
Pain severity was reassessed at weeks 1, 6, 8, and 13.
They assessed the severity of symptoms by Brief Pain
Inventory Short Form, in which pain severity was scored
on a scale of 0
10, with 0 being no pain and 10 being the
worst pain imaginable. This double-blind trial elucidated
the efficacy of Duloxetine in the improvement of pain
associated with CIPN compared with placebo, which is
inconsistent with our findings [39].
In the following comparison of Duloxetine efficacy in
the CIPN, several studies were published before the last
ASCO guideline 2020 for CIPN treatment. In these stud-
ies, the effect of Duloxetine was compared with other
treatments, including Pregabalin [40
42] and vitamin
B12 [31]. So, further data from valid trials were concluded
in the last ASCO CIPN guideline (2020), considering
Duloxetine with further support for treating established
painful CIPN [19].
In our study, better nerve conduction findings in the
intervention group with a prescription of Duloxetine
simultaneous to the start of chemotherapy propose the
prophylactic effect and prevent CIPN theory. Evidence
supporting the potential efficacy of Venlafaxine for the
prevention of Oxaliplatin-induced CIPN [7] provides a
compelling impetus for further study of Venlafaxine or
Duloxetine for preventing CIPN. Aghili
et al
gested the potential efficacy of Duloxetine in preventing
oxaliplatin-induced CIPN. A new NCI-funded clinical
trial is currently undergoing protocol development to
evaluate the efficacy of Duloxetine for the prevention of
Oxaliplatin neuropathy, too [43,44]. Our results suggested
this effect too. Duloxetine downregulates the spinal
expression of both CD11b and GFAP, associated with an
enhancement in sciatic mRNA expression of NGF. Thus,
it could provide peripheral and central neuroprotective
effects, which we detected in the nerve conduction
findings. However, due to the relative risk result, more
studies with electrodiagnosis findings and prolonged fol-
low-up are recommended to evaluate Duloxetine pre-
vention effect on CIPN more.
To our knowledge, it is the first trial that examines the
effect of Duloxetine on the prevention of Paclitaxel
neuropathy based on NCS to date. We obtained com-
plete results demonstrating that Duloxetine affected
subjective parameters of neuropathy in Paclitaxel neu-
rotoxicity, and it also affects neurophysiologic findings.
So, it can be used simultaneously with chemotherapy at
the beginning to prevent neurotoxicity. These findings
add to a growing body of literature on the effectiveness
of Duloxetine. However, we are aware that our research
may have some limitations. Aside from the sample size
due to limited resources, the effect of Duloxetine in com-
parison with other drugs has not been investigated in the
present study. So, a follow-up study is recommended.
In conclusion, 8-week Duloxetine treatment was cor-
related
with
clinically
significant
improvement
in
pain associated with neurotoxicity of Paclitaxel and
improvement of electrodiagnostic findings. However,
recommending Duloxetine as an antineurotoxic agent
in routine regimens requires more detailed clinical tri-
als and mounting evidence with larger samples. We also
recommend long-term researches to evaluate the effects
of Duloxetine on CIPN prevention. Furthermore, it
should be considered in future studies that evaluating
quantitative variables by utilizing NCS-EMG in con-
junction with thorough measurements provides more
holistic information that guides other pathways toward
managing CIPN. Hopefully, the use of Duloxetine
accompanied by other agents will advance the function
and survival of cancer patients.
